candidates.evidence_text:
Flonase is a nasal spray containing fluticasone propionate.
Fluticasone propionate is a corticosteroid that reduces inflammation in the lining of the nose.
Flonase Nasal Spray is used to treat nasal congestion, sneezing, runny nose, and itchy or watery eyes.
These symptoms are caused by seasonal or year-round allergies.
Flonase Allergy Relief is for use in adults and children who are at least 4 years old.
It is available without a prescription.
Children's Flonase Allergy Relief contains the same medicine.
It is also for ages 4 and older.
Flonase Sensimist contains fluticasone furoate rather than fluticasone propionate.
It is approved for use in adults and children 2 years of age and older.
Children's Flonase Sensimist is also for ages 2 and older.
In Flonase Sensimist labeling, relief of itchy, watery eyes applies to ages 12 and older.
The brand-name prescription version of Flonase nasal spray has been discontinued in the United States.
Generic fluticasone propionate nasal spray is still available by prescription.

candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug is used in or approved for the patient population or age group specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Flonase is a nasal spray containing fluticasone propionate.
Fluticasone propionate is a corticosteroid that reduces inflammation in the lining of the nose.
Flonase Nasal Spray is used to treat nasal congestion, sneezing, runny nose, and itchy or watery eyes.
These symptoms are caused by seasonal or year-round allergies.
Flonase Allergy Relief is for use in adults and children who are at least 4 years old.
It is available without a prescription.
Children's Flonase Allergy Relief contains the same medicine.
It is also for ages 4 and older.
Flonase Sensimist contains fluticasone furoate rather than fluticasone propionate.
It is approved for use in adults and children 2 years of age and older.
Children's Flonase Sensimist is also for ages 2 and older.
In Flonase Sensimist labeling, relief of itchy, watery eyes applies to ages 12 and older.
The brand-name prescription version of Flonase nasal spray has been discontinued in the United States.
Generic fluticasone propionate nasal spray is still available by prescription.

candidates.evidence_text:
Before using Flonase Nasal Spray, tell your doctor if you have glaucoma or cataracts.
Tell your doctor if you have liver disease, diabetes, herpes simplex virus of your eyes, tuberculosis, or any other infection.
Tell your doctor if you have sores or ulcers inside your nose.
Tell your doctor if you have recently had injury of or surgery on your nose.
You may start to feel relief on the first day.
It can take several days of regular once-daily use before you get the full effect.
Tell your doctor if your symptoms do not improve within 7 days.
Tell your doctor if you develop new symptoms such as severe facial pain or thick nasal discharge.
Corticosteroids can affect the way your immune system responds to infection.
Avoid being near people who are sick or have infections.
Stop use and ask a doctor if you have, or come into contact with someone who has, chickenpox, measles, or tuberculosis.
Do not administer Flonase Allergy Relief Nasal Spray to a child younger than 4 years old.
Do not administer Flonase Sensimist to a child younger than 2 years.

gt.evidence_text: Tamsulosin is used to treat the symptoms of an enlarged prostate, also called benign prostatic hyperplasia or BPH. These symptoms include a weak urine stream, trouble starting to urinate, dribbling, a feeling of not emptying the bladder completely, needing to urinate often or urgently, and getting up at night to urinate.

candidates.subject: Tamsulosin
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the disease or medical condition specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Tamsulosin is used to treat the symptoms of an enlarged prostate, also called benign prostatic hyperplasia or BPH.
These symptoms include a weak urine stream.
They include trouble starting to urinate.
They include dribbling.
They include a feeling of not emptying the bladder completely.
They include needing to urinate often or urgently.
They include getting up at night to urinate.
Tamsulosin belongs to a group of medicines called alpha blockers.
It works by blocking alpha-1 receptors in the prostate and bladder neck.
Blocking these receptors relaxes the muscle there.
This improves urine flow and eases BPH symptoms.
Tamsulosin is taken once daily, about half an hour after the same meal each day.
Capsules should be swallowed whole and not crushed, chewed, or opened.
The tamsulosin brand name was Flomax.
Flomax has now been discontinued in the U.S.
Generic tamsulosin is available.
Tamsulosin is not approved to treat high blood pressure.
It is not approved for use in women or children.

What are the common side effects of tamsulosin?
:
Common tamsulosin side effects may include:
headache
dizziness
runny or stuffy nose, sore throat, cough, sinus congestion
flu-like symptoms or infection
weakness or lack of energy
back pain, chest pain
diarrhea, nausea
drowsiness or trouble sleeping
tooth problems
abnormal ejaculation, including a smaller amount of semen or no semen at all
reduced interest in sex
blurred vision
Some side effects are more likely at the higher 0.8 mg dose than at the usual 0.4 mg starting dose.
In clinical studies, abnormal ejaculation was reported by about 8 in 100 men taking 0.4 mg.

candidates.evidence_text:
Tamsulosin is broken down in the body mainly by two liver enzymes, CYP3A4 and CYP2D6.
Medicines that block these enzymes can raise the amount of tamsulosin in your blood.
These medicines can increase the risk of side effects.
The medicines block these enzymes.
Do not take tamsulosin with:
strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as ketoconazole
other alpha blockers, such as alfuzosin, doxazosin, prazosin, silodosin, or terazosin
Use with caution, and tell your doctor if you take:
moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as erythromycin
strong CYP2D6 inhibitors, such as paroxetine, or moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors, such as terbinafine
cimetidine
warfarin
medicines for erectile dysfunction or pulmonary arterial hypertension known as PDE5 inhibitors, including avanafil (Stendra), sildenafil (Viagra, Revatio), tadalafil (Adcirca, Cialis), and vardenafil (Levitra).
Taking these with tamsulosin can lower blood pressure enough to cause symptoms.
Some of these cautions matter more at the higher 0.8 mg dose than at 0.4 mg.
Your doctor will decide what is right for you.

They include dribbling.

Tamsulosin is not approved to treat high blood pressure.
It is not approved for use in women or children.

candidates.subject: Tamsulosin
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug has a drug interaction with the drug or substance specified by the object entity that may change effects or cause harm.
candidates.evidence_text:
Tamsulosin is broken down in the body mainly by two liver enzymes, CYP3A4 and CYP2D6.
Medicines that block these enzymes can raise the amount of tamsulosin in your blood.
These medicines can increase the risk of side effects.
The medicines block these enzymes.
Do not take tamsulosin with:
strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as ketoconazole
other alpha blockers, such as alfuzosin, doxazosin, prazosin, silodosin, or terazosin
Use with caution, and tell your doctor if you take:
moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as erythromycin
strong CYP2D6 inhibitors, such as paroxetine, or moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors, such as terbinafine
cimetidine
warfarin
medicines for erectile dysfunction or pulmonary arterial hypertension known as PDE5 inhibitors, including avanafil (Stendra), sildenafil (Viagra, Revatio), tadalafil (Adcirca, Cialis), and vardenafil (Levitra).
Taking these with tamsulosin can lower blood pressure enough to cause symptoms.
Some of these cautions matter more at the higher 0.8 mg dose than at 0.4 mg.
Your doctor will decide what is right for you.

Take once a day, about 30 minutes after the same meal each day.

Swallow the capsule whole.
Do not crush, chew, break, or open it.

Usual adult dose for benign prostatic hyperplasia:
0.4 mg by mouth once a day, taken about half an hour after the same meal each day.
If symptoms have not improved after 2 to 4 weeks at 0.4 mg.

Tamsulosin 0.4 mg should not be taken with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor such as ketoconazole.
If tamsulosin is stopped or interrupted for several days.
Treatment should start again.
The treatment should start at 0.4 mg once a day.

What are the common side effects of tamsulosin?
:
Common tamsulosin side effects may include:
headache
dizziness
runny or stuffy nose, sore throat, cough, sinus congestion
flu-like symptoms or infection
weakness or lack of energy
back pain, chest pain
diarrhea, nausea
drowsiness or trouble sleeping
tooth problems
abnormal ejaculation, including a smaller amount of semen or no semen at all
reduced interest in sex
blurred vision

candidates.subject: Tamsulosin
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug is not indicated or used to treat or manage the condition or situation specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Tamsulosin is used to treat the symptoms of an enlarged prostate, also called benign prostatic hyperplasia or BPH.
These symptoms include a weak urine stream.
They include trouble starting to urinate.
They include dribbling.
They include a feeling of not emptying the bladder completely.
They include needing to urinate often or urgently.
They include getting up at night to urinate.
Tamsulosin belongs to a group of medicines called alpha blockers.
It works by blocking alpha-1 receptors in the prostate and bladder neck.
Blocking these receptors relaxes the muscle there.
This improves urine flow and eases BPH symptoms.
Tamsulosin is taken once daily, about half an hour after the same meal each day.
Capsules should be swallowed whole and not crushed, chewed, or opened.
The tamsulosin brand name was Flomax.
Flomax has now been discontinued in the U.S.
Generic tamsulosin is available.
Tamsulosin is not approved to treat high blood pressure.
It is not approved for use in women or children.

Do not take tamsulosin if you are allergic to tamsulosin or to any of the ingredients in the capsule.
Do not take tamsulosin with other alpha blockers.
Examples of other alpha blockers include alfuzosin (Uroxatral), doxazosin (Cardura), prazosin (Minipress), silodosin (Rapaflo), and terazosin (Hytrin).
Do not take tamsulosin 0.4 mg with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor such as ketoconazole.
These medicines raise tamsulosin levels in your blood.
Tamsulosin can lower your blood pressure when you stand up.
This may make you feel dizzy or faint.
This is most likely when you first start taking it.
This is most likely when your dose changes.
This is most likely when you start it again after a break.
Get up slowly from sitting or lying down.
Be careful driving or doing anything that needs you to be alert until you know how tamsulosin affects you.
In rare cases, tamsulosin can cause priapism.
These cases probably occur in fewer than 1 in 50,000 patients.
Priapism is a painful erection that lasts a long time.
Priapism is not related to sexual activity.

Stop taking tamsulosin and call your doctor at once if you have:

a painful erection that will not go away and is not related to sexual activity
What are the common side effects of tamsulosin?
:

headache
dizziness
runny or stuffy nose, sore throat, cough, sinus congestion
flu-like symptoms or infection
weakness or lack of energy
back pain, chest pain
diarrhea, nausea
drowsiness or trouble sleeping
tooth problems
abnormal ejaculation, including a smaller amount of semen or no semen at all
reduced interest in sex
blurred vision
Some side effects are more likely at the higher 0.8 mg dose than at the usual 0.4 mg starting dose.

candidates.evidence_text:
Do not take tamsulosin if you are allergic to tamsulosin or to any of the ingredients in the capsule.
Do not take tamsulosin with other alpha blockers.
Examples of other alpha blockers include alfuzosin (Uroxatral), doxazosin (Cardura), prazosin (Minipress), silodosin (Rapaflo), and terazosin (Hytrin).
Do not take tamsulosin 0.4 mg with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor such as ketoconazole.
These medicines raise tamsulosin levels in your blood.
Tamsulosin can lower your blood pressure when you stand up.
This may make you feel dizzy or faint.
This is most likely when you first start taking it.
This is most likely when your dose changes.
This is most likely when you start it again after a break.
Get up slowly from sitting or lying down.
Be careful driving or doing anything that needs you to be alert until you know how tamsulosin affects you.
In rare cases, tamsulosin can cause priapism.
These cases probably occur in fewer than 1 in 50,000 patients.
Priapism is a painful erection that lasts a long time.
Priapism is not related to sexual activity.

candidates.subject: Tamsulosin
candidates.relation_definition: The medical condition specified by the subject may present with the symptom specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Do not take tamsulosin if you are allergic to tamsulosin or to any of the ingredients in the capsule.
Do not take tamsulosin with other alpha blockers.
Examples of other alpha blockers include alfuzosin (Uroxatral), doxazosin (Cardura), prazosin (Minipress), silodosin (Rapaflo), and terazosin (Hytrin).
Do not take tamsulosin 0.4 mg with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor such as ketoconazole.
These medicines raise tamsulosin levels in your blood.
Tamsulosin can lower your blood pressure when you stand up.
This may make you feel dizzy or faint.
This is most likely when you first start taking it.
This is most likely when your dose changes.
This is most likely when you start it again after a break.
Get up slowly from sitting or lying down.
Be careful driving or doing anything that needs you to be alert until you know how tamsulosin affects you.
In rare cases, tamsulosin can cause priapism.
These cases probably occur in fewer than 1 in 50,000 patients.
Priapism is a painful erection that lasts a long time.
Priapism is not related to sexual activity.

candidates.subject: Tamsulosin
candidates.relation_definition: The medical condition specified by the subject may present with the symptom specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction, such as hives, itching, rash, swelling of your face, tongue, or throat, or trouble breathing.
Rarely, tamsulosin has been linked to severe skin reactions with blistering and peeling of the skin.
Stop taking tamsulosin and call your doctor at once if you have:
a lightheaded feeling, like you might pass out
a painful erection that will not go away and is not related to sexual activity
What are the common side effects of tamsulosin?
:
Common tamsulosin side effects may include:
headache
dizziness
runny or stuffy nose, sore throat, cough, sinus congestion
flu-like symptoms or infection
weakness or lack of energy
back pain, chest pain
diarrhea, nausea
drowsiness or trouble sleeping
tooth problems
abnormal ejaculation, including a smaller amount of semen or no semen at all
reduced interest in sex
blurred vision
Some side effects are more likely at the higher 0.8 mg dose than at the usual 0.4 mg starting dose.
In clinical studies, abnormal ejaculation was reported by about 8 in 100 men taking 0.4 mg.

Tamsulosin is used to treat the symptoms of an enlarged prostate, also called benign prostatic hyperplasia or BPH.
These symptoms include a weak urine stream.
They include trouble starting to urinate.
They include dribbling.
They include a feeling of not emptying the bladder completely.
They include needing to urinate often or urgently.
They include getting up at night to urinate.
Tamsulosin belongs to a group of medicines called alpha blockers.
It works by blocking alpha-1 receptors in the prostate and bladder neck.
Blocking these receptors relaxes the muscle there.
This improves urine flow and eases BPH symptoms.
Tamsulosin is taken once daily, about half an hour after the same meal each day.
Capsules should be swallowed whole and not crushed, chewed, or opened.
The tamsulosin brand name was Flomax.
Flomax has now been discontinued in the U.S.
Generic tamsulosin is available.
Tamsulosin is not approved to treat high blood pressure.
It is not approved for use in women or children.

other alpha blockers, such as alfuzosin, doxazosin, prazosin, silodosin, or terazosin

moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as erythromycin
strong CYP2D6 inhibitors, such as paroxetine, or moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors, such as terbinafine
cimetidine
warfarin
medicines for erectile dysfunction or pulmonary arterial hypertension known as PDE5 inhibitors, including avanafil (Stendra), sildenafil (Viagra, Revatio), tadalafil (Adcirca, Cialis), and vardenafil (Levitra).
Taking these with tamsulosin can lower blood pressure enough to cause symptoms.
Some of these cautions matter more at the higher 0.8 mg dose than at 0.4 mg.
Your doctor will decide what is right for you.

candidates.evidence_text:
Common side effects:
Common furosemide side effects may include:
diarrhea, constipation, loss of appetite
numbness or tingling
headache, dizziness
blurred vision
redness, bruising, swelling, or pain where a subcutaneous dose is given.
Serious furosemide side effects:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to furosemide, such as hives, difficult breathing, or swelling in your face or throat.
Get emergency medical help if you have a severe skin reaction, such as fever, sore throat, burning eyes, skin pain, or a red or purple skin rash with blistering and peeling.
Furosemide may cause other serious side effects.
Call your doctor at once if you have:
a light-headed feeling, like you might pass out
ringing in your ears, hearing loss
muscle spasms or contractions
pale skin, easy bruising, unusual bleeding
high blood sugar, with increased thirst, increased urination, dry mouth, or fruity breath odor
kidney problems, with swelling, urinating less, feeling tired or short of breath

candidates.subject: Furosemide
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug should be taken or used in the manner specified by the object entity (for example with food or at a fixed time).
candidates.evidence_text:
Take or administer furosemide exactly as prescribed by your doctor.
Follow all directions on your prescription label and read all medication guides or instruction sheets.
Furosemide oral tablets and liquid are taken by mouth.
Measure liquid medicine with the supplied measuring device, not a kitchen spoon.
Furosemide injection is given in a muscle, under the skin, or in a vein.
A healthcare provider will give you this injection if you are unable to take the medicine by mouth.
Using subcutaneous furosemide at home:
You or your caregiver should be trained before your first dose.
You should read the Instructions for Use that comes with your prescription.
Wash your hands first, and check that the liquid is clear and colorless to slightly yellow.
Do not use it if you see particles or if it is cloudy or discolored.
Subcutaneous furosemide is given into the abdomen only.
You should use a different spot on the abdomen each time.
Furoscix ReadyFlow autoinjector
Choose a site at least two inches from your belly button, avoiding skin that is broken or irritated and any scars or stretch marks.

High blood pressure often has no symptoms.

Meloxicam can increase your risk of a fatal heart attack or stroke.
This risk is especially high if you use it long term.
The risk is also higher if you take high doses.
The risk is further increased if you have heart disease.
Even people without heart disease or risk factors could have a stroke or heart attack while taking this medicine.
Do not use this medicine just before or after heart bypass surgery (coronary artery bypass graft, or CABG).
Avoid taking meloxicam after a recent heart attack, unless your doctor tells you to.
You may have an increased risk of another heart attack if you take this medicine after a recent heart attack.
Get emergency medical help if you have chest pain, weakness, shortness of breath, slurred speech, or problems with vision or balance.
Meloxicam may also cause stomach or intestinal bleeding.
This bleeding can be fatal.
These conditions can occur without warning while you are using this medicine, especially in older adults.
Call your doctor at once if you have symptoms of stomach bleeding.
These symptoms include black, bloody, or tarry stools.

Meloxicam can increase your risk of a fatal heart attack or stroke.
Do not use this medicine just before or after heart bypass surgery (coronary artery bypass graft, or CABG).
Meloxicam may also cause stomach or intestinal bleeding.
This bleeding can be fatal.
Meloxicam may also cause stomach or intestinal bleeding.
This bleeding can be fatal.
These conditions can occur without warning while you are using this medicine, especially in older adults.
You should not use meloxicam if you are allergic to it.
You should not use meloxicam if you have ever had an asthma attack or severe allergic reaction after taking aspirin or an NSAID.
To make sure meloxicam is safe for you, tell your doctor if you have ever had:
heart disease, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, diabetes, or if you smoke;
a heart attack, stroke, or blood clot;
ulcers or stomach bleeding;
asthma;
kidney disease (or if you are on dialysis);
liver disease; or
fluid retention
are pregnant or planning a pregnancy
are breastfeeding or intending to breastfeed.

Meloxicam can increase your risk of a fatal heart attack or stroke.
This risk is especially high if you use it long term.
The risk is also higher if you take high doses.
The risk is further increased if you have heart disease.
Even people without heart disease or risk factors could have a stroke or heart attack while taking this medicine.
Do not use this medicine just before or after heart bypass surgery (coronary artery bypass graft, or CABG).
Avoid taking meloxicam after a recent heart attack, unless your doctor tells you to.
You may have an increased risk of another heart attack if you take this medicine after a recent heart attack.
Get emergency medical help if you have chest pain, weakness, shortness of breath, slurred speech, or problems with vision or balance.
Meloxicam may also cause stomach or intestinal bleeding.
This bleeding can be fatal.
These conditions can occur without warning while you are using this medicine, especially in older adults.
Call your doctor at once if you have symptoms of stomach bleeding.
These symptoms include black, bloody, or tarry stools.

candidates.evidence_text:
Meloxicam can increase your risk of a fatal heart attack or stroke.
This risk is especially high if you use it long term.
The risk is also higher if you take high doses.
The risk is further increased if you have heart disease.
Even people without heart disease or risk factors could have a stroke or heart attack while taking this medicine.
Do not use this medicine just before or after heart bypass surgery (coronary artery bypass graft, or CABG).
Avoid taking meloxicam after a recent heart attack, unless your doctor tells you to.
You may have an increased risk of another heart attack if you take this medicine after a recent heart attack.
Get emergency medical help if you have chest pain, weakness, shortness of breath, slurred speech, or problems with vision or balance.
Meloxicam may also cause stomach or intestinal bleeding.
This bleeding can be fatal.
These conditions can occur without warning while you are using this medicine, especially in older adults.
Call your doctor at once if you have symptoms of stomach bleeding.
These symptoms include black, bloody, or tarry stools.

gt.evidence_text: Hydrocodone and acetaminophen is a strong prescription combination pain medicine containing an opioid, hydrocodone, in addition to acetaminophen, which is used to manage moderate to moderately severe pain, when other pain treatments such as non-opioid pain medicines do not treat your pain well enough, or you cannot tolerate them.

candidates.subject: hydrocodone bitartrate and acetaminophen
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug product contains the active ingredient specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Hydrocodone and acetaminophen is a strong prescription combination pain medicine.
The medicine contains an opioid, hydrocodone.
The medicine also contains acetaminophen.
Acetaminophen is used to manage moderate to moderately severe pain.
This medicine is used when other pain treatments do not treat your pain well enough.
It is also used when you cannot tolerate other pain treatments.
Other pain treatments include non-opioid pain medicines.
An opioid pain medicine that can put you at risk for overdose and death.
You are at risk for opioid addiction, abuse, and misuse that can lead to death.
This risk exists even if you take your dose correctly as prescribed.
Hydrocodone and acetaminophen is a Schedule II controlled substance.
All branded hydrocodone and acetaminophen (Norco, Vicodin, Lortab, Hycet, Lorcet, Verdrocet, Xodol, Zamicet) have been discontinued.
Generic hydrocodone and acetaminophen tablets and oral solution is still available.
Hydrocodone and acetaminophen first gained FDA approval on May 3, 1982.

Adult Dose of Hydrocodone And Acetaminophen for Moderate to Severe Pain:
Hydrocodone 2.5 mg-acetaminophen 325 mg per tablet, Hydrocodone 5 mg-acetaminophen 325 mg per tablet:
Initial dose: 1 to 2 tablets every 4 to 6 hours as needed for pain
Maximum dose: 8 tablets/24 hours
Hydrocodone 7.5 mg-acetaminophen 325 mg, Hydrocodone 10 mg-acetaminophen 325 mg per tablet:
Initial dose: 1 tablet every 4 to 6 hours as needed for pain
Maximum dose: 6 tablets/24 hours
Hydrocodone 7.5 mg-acetaminophen 325 mg per 15 mL oral solution:
Initial dose: 15 mL every 4 to 6 hours as needed for pain
Maximum dose: 90 mL/24 hours
Hydrocodone 10 mg-acetaminophen 300 mg per 15 mL oral solution:
Initial dose: 11.25 mL every 4 to 6 hours as needed for pain
Maximum dose: 67.5 mL/24 hours
Comments:
Doses should be individually titrated.
The titration should provide adequate analgesia.
The titration should minimize adverse reactions.
The lowest effective dose should be used.
The dose should be used for the shortest duration.
The duration should be consistent with individual patient treatment goals.

Your caregiver must still get emergency medical help.

A bowel blockage or a narrowing of the stomach or intestines
Signs of an allergy, such as a rash

Before taking hydrocodone and acetaminophen, tell your healthcare provider if you have a history of:
Head injury, seizures
Liver, kidney, thyroid problems
Problems urinating
Pancreas or gallbladder problems
Abuse of street or prescription drugs, alcohol addiction, or mental health problems.
Tell your healthcare provider if you are:
Pregnant or planning to become pregnant.

Breastfeeding.
Hydrocodone and acetaminophen pass into breast milk and may harm your baby.

Hydrocodone and acetaminophen is a strong prescription combination pain medicine.
The medicine contains an opioid, hydrocodone.
The medicine also contains acetaminophen.
Acetaminophen is used to manage moderate to moderately severe pain.
This medicine is used when other pain treatments do not treat your pain well enough.
It is also used when you cannot tolerate other pain treatments.
Other pain treatments include non-opioid pain medicines.
An opioid pain medicine that can put you at risk for overdose and death.
You are at risk for opioid addiction, abuse, and misuse that can lead to death.
This risk exists even if you take your dose correctly as prescribed.
Hydrocodone and acetaminophen is a Schedule II controlled substance.
All branded hydrocodone and acetaminophen (Norco, Vicodin, Lortab, Hycet, Lorcet, Verdrocet, Xodol, Zamicet) have been discontinued.
Generic hydrocodone and acetaminophen tablets and oral solution is still available.
Hydrocodone and acetaminophen first gained FDA approval on May 3, 1982.

Severe asthma, trouble breathing, or other lung problems
A bowel blockage or a narrowing of the stomach or intestines
Signs of an allergy, such as a rash
Are allergic to any of its ingredients.
Before taking hydrocodone and acetaminophen, tell your healthcare provider if you have a history of:
Head injury, seizures
Liver, kidney, thyroid problems
Problems urinating
Pancreas or gallbladder problems
Abuse of street or prescription drugs, alcohol addiction, or mental health problems.
Tell your healthcare provider if you are:
Pregnant or planning to become pregnant.

Breastfeeding.

candidates.relation_definition: The subject treatment or group resulted in the specified average weight loss.
candidates.evidence_text:
Patients on Tirzepatide 15 mg weekly lost an average of 20.9% or 48.6 lb of their body weight after 72 weeks.
This data comes from the Zepbound Study 1 (NCT04184622).
Placebo patients lost an average of 3.1% or 7.2 lb.
Study 1 was a 72-week trial.
The trial compared Zepbound weight loss with placebo.
The trial included adults with obesity or overweight with at least one weight-related condition.
The trial excluded patients with type 2 diabetes.

Treatment dose | Average % weight loss | Average weight lost | Average starting weight
Zepbound 5 mg | 15.0% | 34.0 lb | 226.9 lb
Zepbound 10 mg | 19.5% | 45.5 lb | 233.2 lb
Zepbound 15 mg | 20.9% | 48.6 lb | 232.8 lb
Placebo | 3.1% | 7.2 lb | 231.0 lb

candidates.subject: Mounjaro
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug was evaluated in the clinical trial specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
In the Mounjaro prescribing information, SURPASS-1 (NCT03954834) was a 40-week trial.
The trial was in adults with type 2 diabetes.
The adults had blood sugar that was not adequately controlled with diet and exercise alone.
Patients received once-weekly Mounjaro 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg, or placebo.
After 40 weeks, 78% to 85% of adults taking Mounjaro achieved an HbA1c below 7%.
This is compared with 23% of adults taking a placebo.
The average HbA1c change was -1.8% with Mounjaro 5 mg.
The average HbA1c change was -1.7% with Mounjaro 10 mg.
The average HbA1c change was -1.7% with Mounjaro 15 mg.
The average HbA1c change was -0.1% with placebo.

candidates.subject: Mounjaro
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug or group had the specified percentage of cardiovascular events.
candidates.evidence_text:
SURPASS-CVOT randomized 13,299 adults with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease.
The adults were randomized to Mounjaro (tirzepatide, up to 15 mg once weekly) or dulaglutide 1.5 mg once weekly.
Dulaglutide is a GLP-1 medicine already approved to reduce cardiovascular risk.
The study had a median follow-up of about 4 years.
Cardiovascular death, non-fatal heart attack, or non-fatal stroke occurred in 12.1% of those taking Mounjaro.
These events occurred in 13.0% of those taking dulaglutide.
The hazard ratio was 0.92 with a 95% CI of 0.83–1.01.
The results met the trial's goal of non-inferiority.
The results did not demonstrate superiority.
Death from any cause occurred in 8.5% of the Mounjaro group.
Death from any cause occurred in 10.1% of the dulaglutide group.
The hazard ratio was 0.84 with a 95% confidence interval of 0.75–0.94.
This outcome was not a primary endpoint.
This outcome was not adjusted for multiple comparisons.
Therefore, the result should be read as exploratory.
These results describe how Mounjaro performs against another GLP-1.

gt.entity_2: dual GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonists
gt.evidence_text: Tirzepatide is a dual GIP/ GLP-1 receptor agonist, meaning it activates two gut hormone receptors that help regulate appetite, digestion, and blood sugar. It works by reducing appetite, increasing feelings of fullness, slowing gastric emptying, boosting insulin release when blood sugar is high, and reducing glucagon secretion.

candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological or therapeutic drug class specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
This approval applies to adults with type 2 diabetes.
It applies to those who are at high risk for these events.
Tirzepatide is a dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist.
It activates two gut hormone receptors.
These receptors help regulate appetite, digestion, and blood sugar.
It works by reducing appetite.
It increases feelings of fullness.
It slows gastric emptying.
It boosts insulin release when blood sugar is high.
It reduces glucagon secretion.
Tirzepatide is self-administered as a subcutaneous (under the skin) injection using a single-dose pen, KwikPen, or vial with syringe.
It should always be used together with diet and exercise.
Tirzepatide should not be used in people with type 1 diabetes.
It is not known if tirzepatide is safe in people who have had pancreatitis.

Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor.

One dose is injected weekly (subcutaneously).
For your weekly dose, you need to turn the dose knob all the way until it stops.

After 4 doses, throw away (discard) the Pen, including the unused medicine.
The Pen will prevent you from dialing a full dose after you have given yourself 4 weekly doses.
Do not inject the leftover medicine.
Do not transfer the leftover medicine from your Pen into a syringe.

Common Side Effects:
The most common tirzepatide side effects are:
Diarrhea
Vomiting
Constipation
Nausea (mild to moderate)
Decreased appetite
Abdominal pain.
Serious side effects:
Tirzepatide can cause serious side effects.
Call your doctor right away if you have any of the following:
Stop taking tirzepatide and call your healthcare provider immediately if you have severe pain in your stomach area that will not go away.
This applies if the pain occurs with or without vomiting.
This also applies if the pain spreads to your back.
Severe stomach pain is a sign of pancreatitis.
Diarrhea, nausea, and vomiting can cause dehydration.
Dehydration may lead to kidney problems.
Drink plenty of fluids to reduce this risk.
Tell your doctor if you are unable to keep fluids down.
Gallbladder problems include severe upper stomach pain.
They include fever.
They include nausea.
They include vomiting.
They include yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice).
They include clay-colored stools.
Serious allergic reactions require seeking emergency medical attention.

candidates.evidence_text:
Usual Zepbound Dose for Weight Loss and OSA (Adult):
Initial dose: 2.5 mg under the skin (subcutaneously) once a week.
After 4 weeks: The dosage should be increased to 5 mg subcutaneously once a week.
Further dose increases may occur after at least 4 weeks on the current dose.
The dosage may be increased in 2.5 mg increments.
Recommended maintenance dose for weight loss: 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg injected subcutaneously once weekly.
Recommended maintenance dose for OSA: 10 mg or 15 mg injected subcutaneously once weekly.
Maximum dose: 15 mg subcutaneously once a week.
Dose of Mounjaro for Type 2 Diabetes (Adults and Children 10 Years and Older):
Initial dose: 2.5 mg subcutaneously once a week.
Additional glycemic control is needed.
Increase the dose in 2.5 mg increments after at least 4 weeks on the current dose.
Maximum dose (adults): 15 mg subcutaneously once a week.
Maximum dose (children 10 years and older): 10 mg subcutaneously once a week.
Comments: The starting dose and escalation schedule are designed to reduce the risk of gastrointestinal side effects.

This risk reduction applies to those with type 2 diabetes at high risk.
Zepbound (tirzepatide) is FDA-approved for weight loss and weight management in adults with obesity.
It is also approved for overweight adults with at least one weight-related medical condition.
Zepbound is also approved to treat moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) in adults with obesity.
Mounjaro (tirzepatide) is FDA-approved for type 2 diabetes in adults and children aged 10 years and older.
It is used to help improve blood sugar (glucose) levels.
It is used alongside diet and exercise.
It is also approved to lower the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events.
These events include cardiovascular death, non-fatal heart attack, or non-fatal stroke.

Initial dose: 2.5 mg under the skin (subcutaneously) once a week.

The dosage may be increased in 2.5 mg increments.

Maximum dose: 15 mg subcutaneously once a week.

Maximum dose (adults): 15 mg subcutaneously once a week.
Maximum dose (children 10 years and older): 10 mg subcutaneously once a week.

candidates.evidence_text:
This approval applies to adults with type 2 diabetes.
It applies to those who are at high risk for these events.
Tirzepatide is a dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist.
It activates two gut hormone receptors.
These receptors help regulate appetite, digestion, and blood sugar.
It works by reducing appetite.
It increases feelings of fullness.
It slows gastric emptying.
It boosts insulin release when blood sugar is high.
It reduces glucagon secretion.
Tirzepatide is self-administered as a subcutaneous (under the skin) injection using a single-dose pen, KwikPen, or vial with syringe.
It should always be used together with diet and exercise.
Tirzepatide should not be used in people with type 1 diabetes.
It is not known if tirzepatide is safe in people who have had pancreatitis.

Maximum dose: 15 mg subcutaneously once a week.

Initial dose: 2.5 mg subcutaneously once a week.

Increase the dose in 2.5 mg increments after at least 4 weeks on the current dose.
Maximum dose (adults): 15 mg subcutaneously once a week.
Maximum dose (children 10 years and older): 10 mg subcutaneously once a week.
Comments: The starting dose and escalation schedule are designed to reduce the risk of gastrointestinal side effects.

candidates.evidence_text:
Usual Zepbound Dose for Weight Loss and OSA (Adult):
Initial dose: 2.5 mg under the skin (subcutaneously) once a week.
After 4 weeks: The dosage should be increased to 5 mg subcutaneously once a week.
Further dose increases may occur after at least 4 weeks on the current dose.
The dosage may be increased in 2.5 mg increments.
Recommended maintenance dose for weight loss: 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg injected subcutaneously once weekly.
Recommended maintenance dose for OSA: 10 mg or 15 mg injected subcutaneously once weekly.
Maximum dose: 15 mg subcutaneously once a week.
Dose of Mounjaro for Type 2 Diabetes (Adults and Children 10 Years and Older):
Initial dose: 2.5 mg subcutaneously once a week.
Additional glycemic control is needed.
Increase the dose in 2.5 mg increments after at least 4 weeks on the current dose.
Maximum dose (adults): 15 mg subcutaneously once a week.
Maximum dose (children 10 years and older): 10 mg subcutaneously once a week.
Comments: The starting dose and escalation schedule are designed to reduce the risk of gastrointestinal side effects.

candidates.evidence_text:
In the Mounjaro prescribing information, SURPASS-1 (NCT03954834) was a 40-week trial.
The trial was in adults with type 2 diabetes.
The adults had blood sugar that was not adequately controlled with diet and exercise alone.
Patients received once-weekly Mounjaro 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg, or placebo.
After 40 weeks, 78% to 85% of adults taking Mounjaro achieved an HbA1c below 7%.
This is compared with 23% of adults taking a placebo.
The average HbA1c change was -1.8% with Mounjaro 5 mg.
The average HbA1c change was -1.7% with Mounjaro 10 mg.
The average HbA1c change was -1.7% with Mounjaro 15 mg.
The average HbA1c change was -0.1% with placebo.

candidates.evidence_text:
Do not use this medicine if you have used an MAO inhibitor in the past 14 days.
A dangerous drug interaction could occur.
MAO inhibitors include isocarboxazid, linezolid, methylene blue injection, phenelzine, rasagiline, selegiline, tranylcypromine, and others.
You should not take this medicine if you are allergic to it or if you have ever had:
a seizure disorder;
an eating disorder such as anorexia or bulimia; or
if you have suddenly stopped using alcohol, seizure medication, or a sedative (such as Xanax, Valium, Fiorinal, Klonopin, and others).
Do not take this medicine to treat more than one condition at a time.
If you take bupropion for depression, do not also take this medicine.
Do not take this medicine to quit smoking.
Do not take this medicine for weight management.
Tell your doctor about all of your medical conditions and the drugs you use.
To make sure this medicine is safe for you, tell your doctor if you have ever had:
a head injury, seizures, or brain or spinal cord tumor;
narrow-angle glaucoma;
heart disease, high blood pressure, or a heart attack;
diabetes;

You should not take this medicine if you are allergic to it or if you have ever had:
a seizure disorder;
an eating disorder such as anorexia or bulimia; or
if you have suddenly stopped using alcohol, seizure medication, or a sedative (such as Xanax, Valium, Fiorinal, Klonopin, and others).
Do not take this medicine to treat more than one condition at a time.
If you take bupropion for depression, do not also take this medicine.
Do not take this medicine to quit smoking.
Do not take this medicine for weight management.
Tell your doctor about all of your medical conditions and the drugs you use.
To make sure this medicine is safe for you, tell your doctor if you have ever had:
a head injury, seizures, or brain or spinal cord tumor;
narrow-angle glaucoma;
heart disease, high blood pressure, or a heart attack;
diabetes;

candidates.evidence_text:
Is prednisone a steroid?
:
Yes.
Prednisone is a corticosteroid, also called a glucocorticoid.
Corticosteroids are copies of hormones your adrenal glands make naturally.
They work by lowering inflammation and immune activity.
They are not the same as the anabolic steroids some athletes misuse to build muscle.
How long does it take for prednisone to work?
:
Prednisone starts to be absorbed within about an hour.
Many people notice a difference in symptoms such as swelling, pain, or wheezing within a few hours to a day.
Some conditions take several days or longer to respond.
Delayed-release tablets are designed to release the medicine about four hours after you take them.
Therefore, the timing of your dose matters.
How long does prednisone stay in your system?
:
Prednisone and prednisolone have a half-life of about 2 to 3 hours.
This means half of a dose leaves your blood in that time.
Most of a single dose is out of your bloodstream within about a day.
The effect lasts longer than the drug itself.
A single dose of prednisone quiets your own adrenal glands.

There is no single standard dose.

They do this for a problem that will settle.
Examples of such problems include an asthma flare or a severe allergic reaction.

Examples of such problems include an asthma flare or a severe allergic reaction.

A: The maximum daily dose of over-the-counter (OTC) famotidine (Pepcid AC, Zantac 360) in adults and children over 12 years of age is 40 mg per day unless your doctor prescribes it otherwise. cyclosporine;
lithium;
methotrexate;

heart or blood pressure medication, including a diuretic or "water pill"; or
steroid medicine (such as prednisone)
digoxin.

Ask a doctor or pharmacist if this medicine is safe to use if you have ever had:
heart disease, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, diabetes, or if you smoke;
a heart attack, stroke, or blood clot;
stomach ulcers or bleeding;
liver or kidney disease;
asthma; or
if you take aspirin to prevent heart attack or stroke.

This delay can make it harder to get pregnant.
Tell your doctor if you are having trouble getting pregnant.

Ibuprofen is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID).
It works by reducing hormones that cause inflammation and pain in the body.
Ibuprofen is used to reduce fever.

Ibuprofen is used in adults and children.

Ibuprofen is also available on a prescription from a doctor and may be prescribed at a higher strength (600 mg or 800 mg every 6 hours) for severe pain.

You may have breathing problems or withdrawal symptoms if you start or stop taking certain other medicines.
Tramadol is broken down by two liver enzymes called CYP3A4 and CYP2D6.
Medicines that block or speed up these enzymes change how much tramadol and how much of its active form are in your body.
Starting one of these medicines and stopping one both shift the balance.
Tell your doctor whenever you begin or finish a course of an antibiotic, antifungal medication, heart or blood pressure medication, seizure medication, or medicine to treat HIV or hepatitis C.
Many other drugs can be dangerous when used with tramadol.
Tell your doctor if you also use:
medicine for allergies, asthma, blood pressure, motion sickness, irritable bowel, or overactive bladder
other opioid medicines
buprenorphine, butorphanol, nalbuphine, or pentazocine.
These opioids work differently.
They can block tramadol's pain-relieving effect or bring on sudden withdrawal symptoms.
So, they are generally not taken with tramadol.
a benzodiazepine sedative like Valium, Klonopin, or Xanax

Your risk of seizures is higher if you are taking higher doses than recommended.
Seizure risk is also higher in those with epilepsy or a history of seizures.
Seizure risk is also higher in those taking certain antidepressants, other opioids, MAO inhibitors, or other medicines that lower the seizure threshold.
You should not take tramadol if you have significant breathing problems.
You should not take tramadol if you have acute or severe asthma in a setting where you cannot be monitored.
You should not take tramadol if you have a blockage in your stomach or intestines.
You should not take tramadol if you have taken an MAO inhibitor in the past 14 days.
Examples of MAO inhibitors include isocarboxazid, linezolid, methylene blue injection, phenelzine, and tranylcypromine.
Tell your doctor before starting tramadol if you have a head injury or increased pressure inside your skull.
Tramadol should be used with particular care in these situations.
Prescribers are advised not to prescribe tramadol for people who are suicidal or prone to addiction.

candidates.evidence_text:
You may have breathing problems or withdrawal symptoms if you start or stop taking certain other medicines.
Tramadol is broken down by two liver enzymes called CYP3A4 and CYP2D6.
Medicines that block or speed up these enzymes change how much tramadol and how much of its active form are in your body.
Starting one of these medicines and stopping one both shift the balance.
Tell your doctor whenever you begin or finish a course of an antibiotic, antifungal medication, heart or blood pressure medication, seizure medication, or medicine to treat HIV or hepatitis C.
Many other drugs can be dangerous when used with tramadol.
Tell your doctor if you also use:
medicine for allergies, asthma, blood pressure, motion sickness, irritable bowel, or overactive bladder
other opioid medicines
buprenorphine, butorphanol, nalbuphine, or pentazocine.
These opioids work differently.
They can block tramadol's pain-relieving effect or bring on sudden withdrawal symptoms.
So, they are generally not taken with tramadol.
a benzodiazepine sedative like Valium, Klonopin, or Xanax

candidates.evidence_text:

Signs of an allergic reaction to potassium chloride include difficult breathing.
Signs of an allergic reaction to potassium chloride include swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat.

severe throat irritation;
stomach bloating, severe vomiting, severe stomach pain;
high potassium level - nausea, weakness, tingly feeling, chest pain, irregular heartbeats, loss of movement; or

nausea, vomiting, diarrhea;
gas, stomach pain; or
the appearance of a potassium chloride tablet in your stool.

Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
You may report side effects to FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

Tell your doctor about all your current medicines and any you start or stop using, especially:

Hydroxyzine is thought to work by quieting activity in certain deeper regions of the brain.
These regions are located below the outer layer known as the cortex.
It is not a cortical depressant.
It does not work by slowing down the outer layer of the brain.
Some other sedatives work by slowing down the outer layer of the brain.
Hydroxyzine also blocks histamine, a chemical your body releases during an allergic reaction.
This is what relieves itching.
Laboratory and clinical studies have also shown that hydroxyzine relaxes skeletal muscle.
Hydroxyzine widens the airways (bronchodilation).
Hydroxyzine reduces pain.
These are effects that have been observed rather than uses the medicine is approved for.
Hydroxyzine has also been shown to reduce nausea and vomiting.
This is an approved use for the injection.
It is not an approved use for the forms taken by mouth.

candidates.subject: Hydroxyzine
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the disease or medical condition specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Hydroxyzine is a prescription antihistamine.
It is used to treat anxiety and tension.
It is used to treat itching from allergic skin conditions.
It is used for sedation before and after general anesthesia.
It comes in three oral forms:
Hydroxyzine hydrochloride (HCl) tablets in 10 mg, 25 mg, and 50 mg strengths
Hydroxyzine hydrochloride oral solution (a syrup) containing 10 mg in each 5 mL
Hydroxyzine pamoate capsules in 25 mg
There is also a hydroxyzine hydrochloride injection.
It is given into a muscle by a healthcare professional and is never given into a vein or under the skin.
Hydroxyzine is not chemically related to benzodiazepines, phenothiazines, reserpine, or meprobamate.

candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug has a specific effect or behavior in the group of individuals specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Hydroxyzine taken by mouth is approved for three uses.
These are the same for hydroxyzine HCl and hydroxyzine pamoate.
Anxiety and tension.
For symptomatic relief of anxiety and tension linked to psychoneurosis, and as an add-on treatment in physical illnesses where anxiety is present.
Itching from allergic skin conditions.
For managing itching (pruritus) caused by allergic conditions such as long-term hives (chronic urticaria), eczema-type rashes, and rashes caused by contact with an irritant.
It is also used for itching caused by histamine release.
Sedation around surgery.
As a sedative given before a procedure (premedication) and after general anesthesia.
The injection is also approved for nausea and vomiting.
It is usually given in hospital or clinic settings.
It should not be used for nausea and vomiting caused by pregnancy.
Hydroxyzine has not been studied for long-term use in anxiety.
Studies have not assessed whether it still works as an anti-anxiety medicine beyond four months.
Your doctor should review from time to time whether you still need it.

narcotic (opioid) pain medicines
non-narcotic pain medicines
barbiturates

Your doctor will adjust these doses for you individually.
Care is needed if you take other medicines.
These medicines can affect heart rhythm.
They do this by prolonging the QT interval.
These include:
heart rhythm medicines such as quinidine, procainamide, amiodarone, and sotalol
certain antipsychotics such as ziprasidone, iloperidone, clozapine, quetiapine, and chlorpromazine
certain antidepressants such as citalopram and fluoxetine
certain antibiotics such as azithromycin, erythromycin, clarithromycin, gatifloxacin, and moxifloxacin
other medicines such as pentamidine, methadone, ondansetron, and droperidol
Hydroxyzine does not affect atropine or other belladonna alkaloids.
It is not known to interfere with digitalis.

any skin rash, no matter how mild;
painful urination, blood in the urine;
inflammation of your blood vessels - numbness or tingling, skin rash, fever, headache, body aches, night sweats, weight loss, feeling or weak or tired;

candidates.evidence_text:
Take allopurinol exactly as prescribed by your doctor.
Follow all directions on your prescription label and read all medication guides or instruction sheets.
Your doctor may occasionally change your dose.
Take the tablets with a full glass of water.
To reduce your risk of kidney stones, drink 8 to 10 full glasses of fluid every day.
Do this unless your doctor tells you otherwise.
Take allopurinol tablets after meals to help prevent stomach upset.
Allopurinol injection is injected into a vein by a healthcare provider.
The injection is usually only used if you are unable to take medicine by mouth.
You may need frequent medical tests while using this medicine.
You may need these tests even if you have no symptoms.
Your kidney and liver function may also need to be tested.
Your doctor may change your dose if your kidney function changes.
You may have gout attacks when you first start taking allopurinol tablets.
Your doctor may recommend another gout medication to take with allopurinol.
Keep taking the medicine as directed.
Your symptoms may not improve for up to 2 to 6 weeks.

It is also used to treat kidney stones that have come back.
This occurs in people who have high levels of uric acid in their urine.

candidates.relation_definition: The medical condition specified by the subject may present with the symptom specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to allopurinol.
Signs of an allergic reaction to allopurinol include hives, difficult breathing, and swelling in your face or throat.
Get emergency medical help if you have a severe skin reaction.
Signs of a severe skin reaction include fever, sore throat, burning eyes, skin pain, and a red or purple skin rash with blistering and peeling.
Seek medical treatment if you have a serious drug reaction that can affect many parts of your body.
Symptoms may include skin rash, fever, swollen glands, muscle aches, severe weakness, unusual bruising, or yellowing of your skin or eyes.
Allopurinol may cause serious side effects.
Stop using this medicine and call your doctor at once if you have:
any skin rash, no matter how mild;
painful urination, blood in the urine;
inflammation of your blood vessels - numbness or tingling, skin rash, fever, headache, body aches, night sweats, weight loss, feeling or weak or tired;

candidates.object: take with meals to reduce side effects
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug should be taken or used in the manner specified by the object entity (for example with food or at a fixed time).
candidates.evidence_text:
Take allopurinol exactly as prescribed by your doctor.
Follow all directions on your prescription label and read all medication guides or instruction sheets.
Your doctor may occasionally change your dose.
Take the tablets with a full glass of water.
To reduce your risk of kidney stones, drink 8 to 10 full glasses of fluid every day.
Do this unless your doctor tells you otherwise.
Take allopurinol tablets after meals to help prevent stomach upset.
Allopurinol injection is injected into a vein by a healthcare provider.
The injection is usually only used if you are unable to take medicine by mouth.
You may need frequent medical tests while using this medicine.
You may need these tests even if you have no symptoms.
Your kidney and liver function may also need to be tested.
Your doctor may change your dose if your kidney function changes.
You may have gout attacks when you first start taking allopurinol tablets.
Your doctor may recommend another gout medication to take with allopurinol.
Keep taking the medicine as directed.
Your symptoms may not improve for up to 2 to 6 weeks.

Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to allopurinol.
Signs of an allergic reaction to allopurinol include hives, difficult breathing, and swelling in your face or throat.
Get emergency medical help if you have a severe skin reaction.
Signs of a severe skin reaction include fever, sore throat, burning eyes, skin pain, and a red or purple skin rash with blistering and peeling.
Seek medical treatment if you have a serious drug reaction that can affect many parts of your body.
Symptoms may include skin rash, fever, swollen glands, muscle aches, severe weakness, unusual bruising, or yellowing of your skin or eyes.
Allopurinol may cause serious side effects.
Stop using this medicine and call your doctor at once if you have:
any skin rash, no matter how mild;
painful urination, blood in the urine;
inflammation of your blood vessels - numbness or tingling, skin rash, fever, headache, body aches, night sweats, weight loss, feeling or weak or tired;

Allopurinol is used to treat gout.
Gout is a type of arthritis.

Uric acid is a naturally occurring substance in the body.
The buildup of uric acid causes sudden attacks of redness, swelling, pain, and heat.
These attacks occur in one or more joints.

This happens in people with certain types of cancer.

It is also used to treat kidney stones that have come back.
This occurs in people who have high levels of uric acid in their urine.

Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to allopurinol.
Signs of an allergic reaction to allopurinol include hives, difficult breathing, and swelling in your face or throat.
Get emergency medical help if you have a severe skin reaction.
Signs of a severe skin reaction include fever, sore throat, burning eyes, skin pain, and a red or purple skin rash with blistering and peeling.
Seek medical treatment if you have a serious drug reaction that can affect many parts of your body.
Symptoms may include skin rash, fever, swollen glands, muscle aches, severe weakness, unusual bruising, or yellowing of your skin or eyes.
Allopurinol may cause serious side effects.

any skin rash, no matter how mild;
painful urination, blood in the urine;
inflammation of your blood vessels - numbness or tingling, skin rash, fever, headache, body aches, night sweats, weight loss, feeling or weak or tired;

any active bleeding; or
a stomach ulcer or bleeding in the brain (such as from a head injury).
Tell your doctor if you have ever had:
an ulcer in your stomach or intestines; or
a bleeding disorder or blood clotting disorder.
Clopidogrel may not work as well.
This may happen if you have certain genetic factors.
These genetic factors affect the breakdown of this medicine in your body.
Your doctor may perform a blood test to make sure clopidogrel is right for you.
This medicine is not expected to harm an unborn baby.
However, taking clopidogrel within 1 week before childbirth can cause bleeding in the mother.
Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant.
You should not breastfeed while using this medicine.

Unstable Angina (UA)/Non-ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (NSTEMI) has a loading dose of 300 mg orally once.
The maintenance dose is 75 mg orally once a day.
The duration of therapy is optimal unknown.
ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI) has an optional loading dose of 300 mg orally once.
The maintenance dose is 75 mg orally once a day, with or without thrombolytics.
The optimal duration of therapy is unknown.
Comments: -Administer this drug in combination with aspirin 75 mg to 325 mg orally once a day.
The benefit of this drug is unknown.
This applies to patients who undergo primary percutaneous coronary intervention.
Uses include prevention of atherothrombotic events.
This applies to patients with non-ST-segment elevation acute coronary syndrome.
This includes patients with UA.
This includes patients with NSTEMI.
This includes those who are to be managed medically.
This includes those who are to be managed with coronary revascularization.
This also applies to patients with STEMI.

candidates.subject: Calciferol
candidates.relation_definition: The subject entity is identified as or is equivalent to the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Ergocalciferol is vitamin D2.
Vitamin D helps your body absorb calcium.
Ergocalciferol is used to treat hypoparathyroidism (decreased functioning of the parathyroid glands).
Ergocalciferol is also used to treat rickets.
Rickets is the softening of the bones caused by vitamin D deficiency.
Ergocalciferol is also used to treat low levels of phosphate in the blood.
Low levels of phosphate in the blood are known as hypophosphatemia.
Ergocalciferol may also be used for purposes not listed in this medication guide.

candidates.subject: Calciferol
candidates.relation_definition: The subject entity performs the function or role specified by the object entity.

candidates.subject: Calciferol
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug is associated with the medical treatment guide specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Certain medications can make it harder for your body to absorb vitamin D.
If you take other medications, take them at least 2 hours before or 2 hours after you take ergocalciferol.
Tell your doctor about all your other medicines, especially:
a diuretic or "water pill"; or
mineral oil (sometimes taken as a laxative).
This list is not complete.
Other drugs may affect ergocalciferol.
These other drugs include prescription and over-the-counter medicines.
These other drugs also include vitamins and herbal products.

candidates.object: dose needs may be different during pregnancy
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug carries a safety warning or precaution about the risk or situation specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
You should not take ergocalciferol if you have had an allergic reaction to vitamin D, or if you have:
high levels of vitamin D in your body (hypervitaminosis D);
high levels of calcium in your blood (hypercalcemia); or
any condition that makes it hard for your body to absorb nutrients from food (malabsorption).
Tell your doctor if you have ever had:
heart disease;
kidney disease; or
an electrolyte imbalance.
Certain forms of ergocalciferol may contain ingredients you should know about.
These ingredients include peanut or soybean oil, sugar, aspartame (phenylalanine), or certain food dyes.
Ask a doctor before using ergocalciferol if you have allergies, diabetes, or phenylketonuria (PKU).
Too much vitamin D could harm an unborn baby.
Your dose needs may be different during pregnancy.
Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or if you become pregnant while taking ergocalciferol.
Ergocalciferol can pass into breast milk.

candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug carries a safety warning or precaution about the risk or situation specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
You should not take ergocalciferol if you have had an allergic reaction to vitamin D, or if you have:
high levels of vitamin D in your body (hypervitaminosis D);
high levels of calcium in your blood (hypercalcemia); or
any condition that makes it hard for your body to absorb nutrients from food (malabsorption).
Tell your doctor if you have ever had:
heart disease;
kidney disease; or
an electrolyte imbalance.
Certain forms of ergocalciferol may contain ingredients you should know about.
These ingredients include peanut or soybean oil, sugar, aspartame (phenylalanine), or certain food dyes.
Ask a doctor before using ergocalciferol if you have allergies, diabetes, or phenylketonuria (PKU).
Too much vitamin D could harm an unborn baby.
Your dose needs may be different during pregnancy.
Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or if you become pregnant while taking ergocalciferol.
Ergocalciferol can pass into breast milk.
It may cause side effects in the nursing baby.
Tell your doctor if you are breast-feeding.
Do not give ergocalciferol to a child without medical advice.

medicine to treat depression;
medicine to treat a psychiatric disorder;
a narcotic (opioid) medication; or
medicine to prevent nausea and vomiting.

This includes prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal products.
Give a list of all your medicines to any healthcare provider who treats you.

candidates.evidence_text:
Ondansetron can cause a serious heart problem.
This risk is especially high if you use certain medicines at the same time.
These medicines include antibiotics, antidepressants, heart rhythm medicine, antipsychotic medicines, and medicines to treat cancer, malaria, HIV or AIDS.
Tell your doctor about all medicines you use, and those you start or stop using during your treatment with ondansetron.
Taking ondansetron while using certain other medicines can cause high levels of serotonin to build up in your body.
This condition is called "serotonin syndrome."
Serotonin syndrome can be fatal.
Tell your doctor if you also use:
medicine to treat depression;
medicine to treat a psychiatric disorder;
a narcotic (opioid) medication; or
medicine to prevent nausea and vomiting.
This list is not complete and many other drugs can interact with ondansetron.
This includes prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal products.
Give a list of all your medicines to any healthcare provider who treats you.

Cyclobenzaprine works by reducing the nerve signals in the brain.
These signals drive muscle tone and spasm.
This reduction allows tight, overactive muscles to relax.
It acts within the central nervous system.
It acts primarily at the level of the brain stem.
It does not act on the muscles themselves.
It does not act at the junction between nerves and muscle.

gt.evidence_text: Cyclobenzaprine works by reducing the nerve signals in the brain that drive muscle tone and spasm, which allows tight, overactive muscles to relax. It acts within the central nervous system, primarily at the level of the brain stem, and does not act on the muscles themselves or at the junction between nerves and muscle. 1,2 Because cyclobenzaprine works through the nervous system in this way, it will not relieve muscle spasm caused by central nervous system disease, such as cerebral palsy or spinal cord disease. 1,2

Sprinkle the contents onto a tablespoon of applesauce.
Swallow the mixture right away.
Do not chew the mixture.
Follow your doctor's dosing instructions very carefully.

Tonmya is taken once daily at bedtime, after brushing your teeth.
Drink a few sips of water first so your mouth is moist.
Place the tablet(s) under your tongue until dissolved.
Do not swallow whole, cut, crush, or chew.
Avoid eating or drinking for at least 15 minutes afterward.
Avoid hot, cold, or acidic drinks until morning.
Avoid talking for about 5 minutes after dosing.

The main long-term concerns with spironolactone are chemical rather than something you would feel.
Over time, it can push your potassium too high.
Over time, it can lower your sodium.
Over time, it can lower your magnesium.
Over time, it can lower your calcium.
Over time, it can raise your blood sugar.
Over time, it can raise your uric acid.

This is why you need regular blood tests for as long as you take it, not just at the start.

These doses were still around five times the highest recommended human dose when adjusted for body size.
Whether this happens in people is not known.
This is not a complete list of side effects.
Others may occur.
Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
You may report side effects to the FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

gt.section_title: What is the usual spironolactone dosage?
gt.evidence_text:
Spironolactone dosage for heart failure:
Treatment starts at spironolactone 25 mg once a day, provided your potassium level is 5.0 mEq/L or lower and your kidney function (eGFR) is above 50. If you tolerate that, the dose may go up to 50 mg once a day. If your potassium rises too high, the dose may drop to 25 mg every other day. If your eGFR is between 30 and 50, your doctor may start you at 25 mg every other day because of the higher risk of high potassium.

candidates.evidence_text:
Is spironolactone a diuretic?
:
Yes.
Spironolactone is a diuretic, or water pill.
It belongs to the group called potassium-sparing diuretics.
It works by blocking aldosterone, a hormone that makes your kidneys hold onto salt and water.
Unlike most water pills, spironolactone makes your body keep potassium in.
Most water pills make you lose potassium.
It is a weaker diuretic than medicines such as furosemide.
Furosemide is one reason it is often given alongside another water pill.
It is often given alongside another water pill rather than instead of one.
Is spironolactone used for acne?
:
Spironolactone is not approved by the FDA for treating acne.
Doctors sometimes prescribe it off-label for hormonal acne in women.
Off-label means a doctor is prescribing a medicine for something other than its approved uses.
Off-label prescribing is legal.
Off-label prescribing is common.
Off-label prescribing means the FDA has not reviewed the medicine for that purpose.
The reason it is used this way relates to how spironolactone works.
Spironolactone blocks aldosterone.

Older adults:
Spironolactone is cleared by the kidneys.
Kidney function tends to fall with age.

Why is spironolactone described as a high-risk medicine?
:
The main reason is the risk of a high potassium level.
A high potassium level can cause a dangerous change in your heart rhythm.
A high potassium level often gives no warning symptoms.
The risk rises if your kidneys do not work well.
The risk rises if you take other medicines that raise potassium.
Several very common medicines raise potassium.
Ibuprofen is a very common medicine that raises potassium.
Some blood pressure tablets are very common medicines that raise potassium.
This risk is manageable.
Blood tests are built into treatment.
Your potassium should be checked within a week of starting spironolactone or changing your dose.
It should be checked regularly after that.
Spironolactone also needs care in pregnancy and in people with liver disease.
